name: Automatic placement.
line: Experimental: a balancer picks the pool from measured load, and moves an isolate that blocks or falls behind.
text: `@isoloop/balancer` is experimental and opt-in. Spawn through it instead of naming a pool, and it puts each isolate in a pool where its measured load fits, within a cap on workers. The kernel never moves anything on its own, and the balancer moves only the isolates spawned through it.

It reads every isolate’s heartbeat: its worker’s lag and the isolate’s own busy time. For work the runtime can’t attribute, such as code that resumes after `await`, the app can report its own busy time and how much work is queued. An isolate that blocks twice within a minute, or crashes, waits in a quarantine pool until it has been quiet; the fourth time, it’s kept apart for good. An isolate the kernel has given up on is left alone until the app restarts it.

A move is a restart: the isolate stops, starts again in its new pool and catches up from the bus, and a visual one is blank until it redraws. The balancer groups by load, not by what belongs together, so place by hand what must fail together or stay apart.
